title: Boost stumps by fitting what is still wrong
brief: Write the negative gradients of two losses, then run gradient boosting with stumps and check that each round lowers the loss by the closed-form amount.
hints: squared_error_neg_grad returns y - F, because the slope of 0.5 * (y - F) ** 2 in F is F - y. The absolute-error version returns np.sign(y - F).

gradient_boost starts from F = np.zeros(n). Each round sets target = neg_grad(y, F), fits _fit_stump(X, target), and updates F = F + learning_rate * _predict_stump(stump, X). Round 1 under squared error fits y itself.

Append {"target": target, "prediction": F.copy()} to the history. Without .copy(), an in-place update changes every earlier entry. On the hand example, F after round 1 with learning_rate 0.5 is [1, 1, 4.5, 4.5].
